highlights.title: Closed linear embeddings of affine algebraic groups
highlights.html: Every affine group scheme locally of finite type over a field K admits a group-scheme morphism into GL_n over K for some natural number n whose underlying scheme morphism is a closed immersion. Nonreduced group schemes are included, with no representation or basis supplied.

highlights.title: Finite Hopf algebras and right Hopf modules
highlights.html: Every finite-dimensional Hopf algebra H over a field K admits a K-linear functional λ whose multiplication pairing (a, x) ↦ λ(a * x) is nondegenerate in both arguments. The Hopf algebra need not be commutative or cocommutative, and no restriction on the characteristic or assumption of antipode bijectivity is required. Over a commutative semiring, a specified right comodule over a possibly noncommutative semiring Hopf algebra with a given compatible right action and scalar tower is linearly equivalent to its coinvariants tensored with that Hopf algebra, without flatness or finiteness assumptions.

The coefficient Hopf algebra need not be commutative and its antipode need not be invertible. For commutative coefficients the twist is identity.

highlights.title: Coherence via kernels of maps from finite free modules
highlights.html: For any unital, possibly noncommutative ring R and any left R-module M, M is coherent (finitely generated with every finitely generated submodule finitely presented) if and only if M is finitely generated and the kernel of every R-linear map Rⁿ → M is finitely generated for every natural number n, including zero.

highlights.title: Finiteness, projectivity and flatness under injective tensor units
highlights.html: Let R be a commutative ring, S an R-algebra and M an additive commutative monoid with its given R-module structure. Assume the canonical unit N → S ⊗[R] N is injective for every additive commutative R-semimodule N in Type (max uR uM). For a possibly noncommutative semiring S, S ⊗[R] M is finitely generated over S if and only if M is finitely generated over R. For a possibly noncommutative ring S, the corresponding finite-presentation equivalence holds. If S ⊗[R] M is finite and projective over any possibly noncommutative semiring S, M is finite and projective over R; finite presentation of M is derived internally. For a commutative ring S, flatness is likewise equivalent. All three carrier universes are independent; S need not be flat over R, and M needs neither an S-action nor a supplied additive group structure.

highlights.title: Internal Krull–Schmidt decompositions and cancellation
highlights.html: Over any possibly noncommutative ring, a Noetherian module or an Artinian module is a finite internal direct sum of nonzero indecomposable submodules, with an explicit A i ≠ ⊥ fact paired with each summand's categorical indecomposability. Two supplied finite internal decompositions of linearly equivalent modules have matching summands up to linear equivalence when all summands have local endomorphism rings. Indecomposable summands and finite length of one total suffice instead. Both matching conclusions include explicit nonzero facts for each supplied family. Arbitrary finite index types use the caller's decidable equality instances and may be empty; existence uses stock equality on Fin n. Matching is existential; no preservation of the given coordinates or canonical choice is asserted. A common finite-length module P, possibly zero, cancels from P × M ≃ₗ[R] P × N with no chain condition on M or N. Zero modules, including those over a zero ring, have the empty decomposition.

highlights.title: Coherence of square-zero extensions and finite-support idealizations
highlights.html: For a division ring D and a bimodule M in independent universes, the trivial square-zero extension D ⋉ M is left coherent if and only if M is finitely generated on the left. Both compatible module actions are retained, without centrality. For the stock pointwise left module ι →₀ D and any compatible right action, this is equivalent to finiteness of ι, including the empty index type. For a field k and infinite ι, the canonical inclusion algebra k → TrivSqZeroExt k (ι →₀ k), a ↦ (a, 0), is faithfully flat but not coherent. The canonical field criterion allows the zero coefficient space; finite generation means finite dimension, not a finite underlying set. More generally, for a possibly noncommutative ring R and a bimodule M with its given commuting left and right actions, left coherence of R ⋉ M implies finite generation of M on the left whenever r ↦ r • v is injective for one vector v. Sufficiency holds for a left coherent base and a coefficient bimodule finitely presented on the left.

deliverables.description: Native continuous group cohomology in low degrees; transfer and compact-group degree-one torsion; finite-level Tate deflation, compact exceptional Tate groups and diagrams, compact finite-bar homology and norm-limit sequences. For compact topological groups with discrete jointly continuous coefficients over a topologized ring, every continuous cohomology class lifts from a finite open-normal quotient with invariant coefficients. In positive degrees a class-dependent quotient order annihilates the class. The native open-normal inflation cocone is a filtered colimit in all degrees, including zero, with the actual cohomology topology and arbitrary topological-module targets. For arbitrary finite index types, finite functions are naturally equivalent to coefficient-left tensors over a commutative semiring; for finite groups, the twisted action agrees with the diagonal left-regular tensor action. This algebraic result gives no continuous or topological-representation equivalence. At each fixed acting group, the degree-zero coefficient functor is naturally isomorphic to invariants over a ring with its supplied topology.

deliverables.name: dedekind-ideal-arithmetic
deliverables.title: Dedekind ideal arithmetic
deliverables.description: Reusable ideal arithmetic, module indices and intrinsic heights of normed invertible modules over rings of integers. Ideal-norm comparisons, principal-prime extraction and class-group localization sit alongside finite section quotients, common scalar multiples, integral-section heights and normalized logarithmic heights, with tensor-product, positive metric-rescaling and equivalence-pullback formulas. Rational frames evaluate the same intrinsic height through coefficient-ideal norms and weighted archimedean products. Nonzero fractional-ideal norms factor as finite-support prime-norm products with signed exponents; over number fields, negative coefficient-ideal exponents give the finite-place numerator of height. Supplied frames extend to linear coordinates over semiring algebras. Over an infinite Dedekind domain with finite quotients, invertible modules have canonical definite ultrametric seminorms on their adic fibres, characterized in every rational frame by the residue cardinality raised to the signed coefficient-ideal count, times the coordinate norm. Principal fractional-ideal counts determine scalar adic valuations and residue-cardinality completion norms. Rank-one seminorm scalar extension, relative-degree formulas for weighted infinite-place products, fractional-ideal norm extension and isometric completion maps supply further interfaces.

highlights.title: Ideal norms, factorization and principal primes
highlights.html: In an infinite commutative Dedekind domain with finite quotients, a nonzero smaller ideal has strictly larger absolute norm, and nested ideals of equal absolute norm coincide. Over a Dedekind domain finite free over the integers, each nonzero fractional-ideal norm is the finite-support product of height-one prime norms raised to signed integer exponents; the fraction field needs no number-field structure. In an infinite Dedekind domain finite free over the integers, a supplied element with prime absolute algebraic norm yields a principal prime above that rational prime. Over any Dedekind domain and fraction field, a nonzero fractional ideal contains a nonzero element whose principal ideal attains the same signed exponent at a fixed height-one prime; the ideal need not be principal.

highlights.title: Class groups under localization
highlights.html: Class extension is surjective for torsion-free localizations of Dedekind domains, and a supplied class generator killed by extension makes the target a principal ideal ring and a unique factorization domain.

highlights.title: Section indices and rational-frame coordinates
highlights.html: Nonzero sections of invertible modules over commutative domains with finite quotients span finite-index submodules; any two nonzero sections of one invertible module over a commutative domain admit a common nonzero scalar multiple. A supplied frame on K tensor_R M extends to an F-linear coordinate on F tensor_R M through compatible algebras over commutative semirings R and K, with F not required commutative, without finiteness or norm hypotheses. A finitely generated module with a supplied frame over a fraction field has a nonzero coefficient fractional ideal; torsion-freeness makes the coefficient map injective, but is not required to construct the ideal.

highlights.title: Intrinsic heights of normed invertible modules
highlights.html: For a number field K, definite seminorms on the archimedean completion fibres of an invertible module over its ring of integers define a positive height equal to the section index divided by the weighted norm product for every nonzero integral section. Ordinary norms have weight one at real places and two at complex places. The normalized logarithmic height is (log index minus the weighted log norm sum) divided by [K:Q]. Tensor metrics multiply heights and add logarithmic heights. Positive placewise rescaling divides height by the weighted factor and subtracts its degree-normalized logarithm; equivalence pullback preserves both heights. Every rational frame evaluates this same height as the reciprocal of the product of its coefficient-ideal norm and the weighted archimedean product at its unit vector. Equivalently, the numerator is the finite-support product of residue cardinalities with negative coefficient-ideal exponents, with no extra finite-place weights. No integral basis is assumed, and only logarithmic height is divided by [K:Q].

highlights.title: Adic fibre seminorms and integral spans
highlights.html: Let R be an infinite Dedekind domain with finite quotients, K its fraction field, p a height-one prime and F = p.adicCompletion K with its selected residue-cardinality norm. An invertible R-module M has a canonical definite ultrametric F-seminorm on F tensor_R M. For every rational frame e and every fibre vector x, its value is q raised to FractionalIdeal.count K p e.coefficientIdeal times the norm of e.fibreCoordinate F x, where q is the residue cardinality. The signed count appears with a plus sign, in contrast to the finite-place height factor. The seminorm is frame-independent and uniquely determined by this weight at the image of e.symm 1. On M = R the whole seminorm is the completion norm composed with the tensor right-unit equivalence; the same vector 1 tensor 1 has value one in every scalar frame. The supplied-frame constructor only needs a finitely generated module and a rational frame, not integral invertibility, freeness or torsion-freeness. No number-field structure, finite-free presentation over the integers, norm on K or norm or metric instance on a fibre is required. Over any Dedekind domain and fraction field, the valuation-integer span of integral sections is the image of the integer tensor fibre and spans the whole field fibre. It is finite for a finite module; flatness makes the image map an equivalence, and the scalar model identifies the whole span with the valuation-integer ring. These algebraic statements need no norm, infinite-ring or finite-quotient hypothesis.

deliverables.name: formal-power-series
deliverables.title: Formal Power Series
deliverables.description: Integral weighted negative logarithmic derivatives of native formal-power-series units over arbitrary commutative rings, with group laws, naturality and finite coefficient formulas; and coefficientwise ideal-adically restricted native multivariate power series with finite polynomial reductions, regular-principal internal kernels. Polynomial completion over any commutative coefficient ring is the algebra of series over its adic completion with polynomial images at every original quotient precision; coefficient transport recovers the original restricted-series ring equivalence for adically complete coefficients. Ideal-preserving coefficient maps and arbitrary variable maps on these completed-coefficient series give functorial ring maps with finite source-row fiber sums, including infinite fibers. The polynomial-completion comparison is natural in both directions, with completed-scalar compatibility and raw row-kernel containment, without original completeness or finiteness assumptions. The restricted subring also has a coefficient-ring algebra structure, all-level surjective scalar-linear polynomial reductions, and regular-principal module-quotient equivalences, including a separate native-integer API for default module instances. Over adically complete coefficient rings, every polynomial linear endomorphism extends to the restricted series, with finite-level and kernel-preserving uniqueness laws. Independently of completeness, coefficientwise reduction kernels multiply into the kernel at the sum of their levels, including finite-sum laws. For adically complete coefficient rings, units of the restricted subring are detected by the first polynomial reduction or by constant and nonconstant coefficient criteria, with no finite-variable restriction. Over finitely many variables, restrictedness has a degree-cutoff criterion; if the coefficient ideal is finitely generated, every reduction kernel is the intrinsic algebraic image ideal of its corresponding ideal power. Separate restricted-series modules add coefficient content, intrinsic actual-ring leading terms, division under adic/valuation hypotheses and conditional ideal generation by a finite primitive family. A generic support leaf compares cofinal ideal-adic filtrations on arbitrary modules. Change-of-ideal maps and surjective polynomial reduction work for arbitrary ideals and variables. Local-ring polynomial residue is compatible with valuation-domain residue; injective first-variable regrouping has polynomial and finite-variable reindexing interfaces. Intrinsic leading products and singleton division have separate Hausdorff uniqueness and complete primitive-existence interfaces; first-variable division yields finite-polynomial remainders. A supplied division of X₀^d by a divisor with regrouped residue degree d and nonzero scalar top, with actual remainder support below d, gives constant-unit quotient residue; radical equality and completeness reflect it to a unit. With a nonzero principal-adic parameter in the maximal ideal of a commutative valuation domain, radical equality and completeness, a restricted series whose regrouped residue polynomial has degree d and nonzero scalar top coefficient admits a unique unit multiplier and monic first-variable polynomial of degree d, even among competing multipliers not assumed units; coefficient primitivity is derived from the top term.

deliverables.name: fundamental-groupoids
deliverables.title: Fundamental Groupoids
deliverables.description: Endomorphism transport, chosen-vertex equivalences and connectedness of fundamental groupoids, with small-path generation and constructed strict descent along arbitrary indexed open covers into arbitrary categories. Based van Kampen for two-open covers with a common basepoint and path-connected opens and intersection, as a unique-homomorphism universal property and a pushout of groups. A path-connected based open core and charts with that common pairwise overlap give a colimit of their inclusion star when the core and charts cover the space. The raw group colimit is multiplicatively equivalent to the ambient fundamental group, preserving every leg in both directions with independent space and index universes. Inclusion-directed covers by neighborhoods of a supplied basepoint give colimits without path connectedness or intersection closure, with a universal property for arbitrary target monoids in independent universes. Monotone neighborhood covers indexed by directed preorders give the same universal property with compatibility only along index inequalities, and colimit data for the canonical preorder diagram. Signed-period additive-circle and complex-circle fundamental groups have integer coordinates, with signed-loop, inverse, endpoint, nonidentity and homeomorphism-compatibility laws, using Mathlib's quotient coverings. Continuous maps act functorially on path components, with equal actions for homotopic maps, in independent space universes without separation assumptions. Based postcomposition on generalized loops and homotopy quotients for every cube-index type, with positive homomorphisms, based-homotopy invariance and fundamental-group compatibility. Homotopy quotients commute with arbitrary dependent products for all cube indices in independent universes, by coordinate evaluation and loop assembly; for nonempty cube indices with decidable equality this is a multiplicative equivalence for the existing group structures. Raw cubical homotopy quotients canonically identify with path components of the same compact-open generalized-loop spaces, naturally in based postcomposition and compatibly with the empty-index comparison. For singleton index types, the generalized-loop space is homeomorphic to the compact-open based path space through Mathlib's singleton-coordinate equivalence, with full forward and inverse evaluation, constant/reflexive-path laws and based-postcomposition naturality. Index and space universes are independent, without separation or local compactness assumptions on the target. The based homotopy-fiber point projection has class image equal to the preimage of the constant class for every cube index, with range–kernel form for the existing positive groups. On whole based quotient hom-sets [Z,-], the original fiber projection, forward-loop inclusion and loop map give three successive range–constant-class preimage identities for every original based source (Z,z0). Ordinary ULift handles independent Z,E,B universes; homotopy is relative to {z0}, with arbitrary ordinary topologies and no geometric hypotheses. The pointed homotopy-fiber chain complex has lifted cubical homotopy quotients of the base, total space and fiber in successive degrees, is exact in the pointed-set sense at every positive chain degree, and admits chain maps for strict based squares. Its incoming differential need not surject onto the terminal path-component term of the base. Equivalences of cube-index types induce quotient equivalences by reindexing representatives, with inverse, identity, composition and based-postcomposition laws in independent universes. For nonempty indices with decidable equality, the same maps are multiplicative for the existing group structures, without requiring corresponding selected axes. The continuous identity from Mathlib's CompHaus-test topology to the original target topology induces a natural equivalence on every cubical homotopy quotient, multiplicative for nonempty indices with decidable equality. Probe, cube-index and target universes are independent. Unchanged functions lift continuously from every universe-parameterized compactly generated source. Ordinary products preserve universe-parameterized compact generation when one factor is locally compact. For such a compactly generated factor P and any topological A, the refinement of P × A is homeomorphic to P times the refinement of A by the identity functions. Supplied relative homotopies from compactly generated sources lift with unchanged joint cylinder functions, endpoints and arbitrary fixed subsets, with counit inverse and naturality laws. Coverings induce canonical quotient-map injections for nonempty cube indices and bijections for nontrivial indices, without decidable equality. For nontrivial indices with decidable equality, the stock homotopy groups are multiplicatively equivalent, with forward postcomposition and inverse represented by a chosen based generalized-loop lift. Coordinate-face cube boundaries are path connected for nontrivial indices, including infinite ones. Finite cube boundaries are closed, including the empty-index case. For every index type, the boundary complement with its subtype topology is homeomorphic to the real product on that type; for finite indices it is locally compact. A Hausdorff space maps continuously to the one-point compactification of any open subspace by retaining that subspace and collapsing its complement to infinity, without a local compactness assumption. Adding a disjoint point gives a surjection, even for the whole space, and a quotient map when the ambient space is compact. For compact Hausdorff ambient spaces, collapse pullback is a homeomorphism between continuous maps based at infinity and ambient maps equal to the chosen point outside the open subspace, with ordinary compact-open/subtype topologies. Its finite-cube specialization identifies generalized loops with based maps from the one-point compactification of the cube-boundary complement, including empty indices and arbitrary topological targets in independent universes. Relative affine interpolation fixes any agreement subset for maps into real modules with continuous addition and scalar multiplication. Generalized loops in such modules are homotopic relative to the cube boundary to their constant loops, and all their homotopy quotients are subsingletons, including empty indices and arbitrary chosen points. Generic covering-map lifting and based equivalences, monodromy, equivariant fiber maps and deck-group centralizers. A covering map is proper exactly when every point fiber is finite, without separation, local compactness or uniform-degree assumptions. Fiber finiteness is locally constant, with clopen locus including empty fibers and excluding infinite ones. On a preconnected base, properness is equivalent to finiteness of the fiber at any given point. For preconnected total space and a supplied total-space point, finiteness of its fiber suffices without base connectedness or surjectivity. With path-connected total space, monodromy identifies the based fiber with left cosets of the induced image, and properness is equivalent to that subgroup having finite index. The canonical comparison from the categorical coproduct of fundamental groupoids to the fundamental groupoid of the topological coproduct is an equivalence, for arbitrary families without connectivity assumptions. Semilocal simple connectivity uses chosen-center loops contracting in the ambient space, with induced-map reflection, local-homeomorphism transport, covering consequences and a locally path-connected neighborhood refinement. Radial deformations of punctured closed and open balls onto spheres are available in arbitrary real normed spaces. Positive real scaling identifies Circle with each positive-radius complex sphere. Scaling and normalization give strict retractions and circle-fixing deformations of punctured balls. Ordered two-factor based wedges are strictly isomorphic to binary wedges, and both nested binary three-factor wedges flatten strictly to the finite wedge. Forward and inverse maps preserve the ordered factor inclusions and common point, for possibly different factors in an arbitrary common universe. In the named cartesian structure on the ordinary opposite based-homotopy category, the unop of the associator followed by left-nested flattening equals right-nested flattening after applying the quotient functor. Positive-radius inner circles classify punctured complex-ball fundamental groups by the integers, with normalization and scaling maps and a nontrivial positive generator. Compatible functions on a disk attachment descend uniquely to any target type, and continuous descent has the same underlying function. Removing the centres of an arbitrary family of attached closed complex unit disks gives a subspace that strongly deformation retracts onto the original space image, for arbitrary unbased circle maps and independent space and disk-index universes, without connectivity or separation assumptions. For a selected attaching map taking 1 to a chosen point, the punctured component has a path-connected thickened chart with contractible disk piece and punctured-open-disk overlap. Its positive half-radius generator retracts to the positive attaching loop class. For an entirely based family, these charts and the core form an Option-indexed open cover of the attachment component with path-connected members and pairwise intersections, including the empty disk family. Commuting squares of source and target homeomorphisms induce homeomorphisms of ordinary compact-open homotopy fibers at corresponding specified points, with point, full-path, inverse, identity, composition and projection laws. Fibers of product maps are homeomorphic to products of ordinary homotopy fibers, preserving both retained source points and full same-time paths, naturally for arbitrary continuous squares in independent universes. A free source factor splits from the fiber of f composed with first projection: the result is HomotopyFiber f b times the free factor, retaining both source coordinates and the entire original path. Whole continuous-map diagrams, inverse and constructor laws and same-time evaluation hold for arbitrary topologies in three independent universes; arbitrary-square naturality with a continuous free-factor map uses six independent universes. For f equal to identity, the full identity-fiber factor remains.

deliverables.description: Finite general linear groups over possibly noncommutative semirings and rings: Kronecker products of matrix units with reversed identity-factor inverse witnesses, elementary units, ordered commutators, relative normal closures inside elementary groups, finite stabilization, Whitehead block factorization and doubled relative membership and lifting; rectangular block units for independent finite indices with explicit diagonal units; reindexing, nil and quasiregular ideals, congruence subgroups and quotient lifting, nonunital unitization, and matrix trace modulo additive commutators. Scalar unit reflection for Ring-to-Semiring homomorphisms forces quasi-regularity of the canonical two-sided kernel without surjectivity; for surjective maps it is equivalent to this kernel condition. Source and target universes are independent, with no commutativity or local-ring hypothesis. A square-zero kernel of any Ring-to-Semiring homomorphism identifies units mapping to 1 with the additive kernel via u - 1 and 1 + x; the inverse unit has value 1 - x. All mixed kernel products must vanish, with no surjectivity assumption. For left ideals I, J with I^2 contained in J, original-ring principal units map to the additive layer I/(I intersect J); Jacobson containment of I makes the map surjective and identifies its kernel quotient with that layer. Neither two-sidedness nor J contained in I is required. Dual-number GL, SL and scalar-unit reduction kernels, determinant/trace, coefficient maps and the left-conjugation adjoint action use commutative rings. The trace quotient is an additive group, not a quotient ring; its corner inverse requires a chosen matrix index. A Steinberg presentation adds elementary-symbol relations, universal lifts and a finite map onto the elementary subgroup, without opposite-root or central-extension assertions. Over iterated dual numbers, Mathlib's GL units have an ordered commutator equal to the mixed lift of the associative matrix bracket; its outer reduction-kernel element has complete pure-inner readback. For trace-zero inputs, the refinement in Mathlib's SL group uses special-linear factors, identifies the ordered mixed commutator and reads back its pure-inner trace-zero coefficient in the outer SL kernel. Elementary unit-pivot diagonalization, product-one diagonal membership, continuous elementary paths and finite special-linear elementary neighborhoods add algebraic and topological interfaces with their respective unit-minor, path-connectedness and open-scalar-unit hypotheses. Zero-product rectangular blocks over any ring yield a unit 1 + AB whose stabilization is an elementary ordered commutator of block shears. Stable general linear groups form a direct limit over semirings; over rings their stable elementary subgroup is perfect and equals the commutator subgroup, with quotient canonically the abelianization. Over commutative rings the stable determinant and its quotient and abelianization factorizations admit rank-one sections; the elementary subgroup lies in the determinant kernel. Ordered products of matrices with entries in a left ideal I over a semiring have entries in I raised to the list length, for independent finite decidable indices, including empty lists and indices. Repeated factors recover the matrix-power bound. Any exponent annihilating the whole ideal also annihilates a matrix whose entries lie in it.

Empty support and infinite fiber dimensions are included. For two arbitrary preorder subsets, the tagged lexicographic union has the maximum of their dimensions and their sum plus one. For arbitrary subsets of independently universed dependent sums with raw relations, chain height is the supremum of finite sums of fiber heights, assuming only pairwise comparability and irreflexivity of the active indices. Empty fibers and infinite heights are allowed, with no transitivity, global order, finiteness or attainment hypothesis.

highlights.title: Dimension and point ranks of finite dependent lexicographic products
highlights.html: For arbitrary subsets of independently universed given preorders over a finite linearly ordered index, lexicographic dimension is the WithBot map of ENat decrement applied to the product of the shifted fibre dimensions. Product and addition are in WithBot ENat, with only the decrement in ENat. Empty index, empty fibres and infinite dimensions are included. The canonical partial order is equality or strict lexicographic comparison with equality prefixes; it needs only strict less-than relations on the fibres and agrees as a whole record with Mathlib's construction when the fibres have partial orders. For a given section of arbitrary given fibre preorders, height and coheight are sums of the original coordinate ranks weighted by the strict-chain vertex heights of whole later fibres. Both use the same original suffix priority. These ENat formulas include empty indices and unattained infinite heights, with no fibre partial-order, linearity, finiteness or extra inhabitation premise.

deliverables.title: Projective modules
deliverables.description: Row-finite linear systems with target satisfying Module.Baer have full solutions whenever every finite set of rows has a solution. Over a semisimple ring this holds for every left module, including modules over division rings; scalars, targets, rows and coordinates have independent universes. Solutions are arbitrary coordinate functions, not necessarily finitely supported functions. Reusable Lean theory of projective modules: finite-projective dual and evaluation base change, invertible modules, exterior algebras and powers, determinants, bounded cancellation and countable absorption, infinite free coordinates, finite stable presentations and IBN-only integer-rank independence, balanced tensor products, right scalar extension and chosen right-free coefficient transport along arbitrary unital semiring homomorphisms, exactness, local and PID freeness, preadditive stable module categories, countably generated submodules over left-Noetherian rings, and locally constant rank and componentwise-free classification. Noncommutative and commutative results retain their distinct hypotheses; rank classification is not asserted for all finite projectives over arbitrary rings. Given an equivalence of module categories over arbitrary rings, finite generation is preserved and reflected with independent scalar and carrier universes. Finite projectivity is preserved with an unrestricted source carrier and target carrier at its scalar/carrier maximum, and is reflected when both carriers are at their corresponding maxima. No linearity, commutativity or freeness premise is imposed on this equivalence interface. Scalar and source universes are independent; no right action on M, additive inverses or freeness is assumed. Evaluation, inverse and naturality laws accompany the equivalence. If the module is an additive commutative group, additivity and cyclicity give trace zero on additive commutators; no ring structure on the scalar semiring is required. For two finite projective additive-commutative-monoid modules, tensoring endomorphisms multiplies their traces, with independent scalar and factor universes. Both bilinear and pointwise forms are provided. Partial trace over a finite projective factor M contracts arbitrary linear maps M tensor N → M tensor P to maps N → P, linearly in the whole input. The untraced factors are arbitrary, with four independent universes. On a tensor product of maps a and b it is trace(a) times b, without normalization. On nonfree projectives the scalar trace need not be a natural multiple of the scalar unit. Product endomorphisms have the sum of their factor traces; diagonal inclusion-projection blocks have the factor traces and off-diagonal blocks have trace zero. An arbitrary block endomorphism of a product of finite projective factors has the sum of its diagonal traces. The off-diagonal formulas assume finite projectivity only of the product, without bases, additive inverses or coupled carrier universes. An arbitrary endomorphism of a finite dependent product of finite projective modules has the finite sum of the traces of its diagonal coordinate composites. The index need only be finite, with independent scalar, index and carrier universes. Over arbitrary rings, the library also describes stably-free kernels of surjections onto finitely generated stably-free targets, finite-coordinate kernel presentations and surjective right-linear matrix kernels. Rectangular right-coordinate maps need finite source coordinates but allow arbitrary target indices; transporting a supplied equivalence needs both indices finite. These constructions use left coefficients and right scalars, without commutativity, injectivity, IBN or equal index cardinalities. Finite projective categories over arbitrary rings are essentially small in the ring universe at independent carrier universes. Ring-universe representatives and linear equivalences give a common reference skeleton for comparing arbitrary input classes. Over a commutative semiring, an idempotent-generated ideal is free exactly for the zero and unit idempotents, without a nontriviality assumption. Right scalar-extension comparisons satisfy pointwise unit and triple-composition associativity laws over arbitrary rings and right modules, with five independent scalar and module universes. A unit semiconjugating two homomorphisms of arbitrary rings induces a fixed-right-target linear equivalence on their scalar extensions, with left multiplication by the unit and its inverse on tensor coefficients. Principal right ideals over arbitrary source and target rings have an image-one scalar-extension equivalence without idempotence, and an image-zero annihilation theorem with idempotence. An idempotent right ideal and its scalar extension are bundled as finite projectives over arbitrary rings, including noncentral matrix idempotents. The right-ideal bundle has an identity linear equivalence to its canonical principal ideal, identifying zero and scalar action. Canonical right regular modules on ordinary semiring carriers are finite and free, including zero semirings. A finite projective common stabilizer can be replaced by a common standard finite free one, without finiteness or projectivity assumptions on the ambient modules. Finite ranks are preserved by ring-universe representatives; finitely generated free categorical objects are classified by finite rank over rings satisfying the strong rank condition, not all finite projectives over arbitrary rings. Finite projective right-module classes form a ring-sized direct-sum monoid and additive Grothendieck group, with arbitrary-carrier generators, universal properties and common finite-projective or finite-free stabilization criteria over arbitrary rings. Over division rings, canonical natural-valued class and integer-valued group dimensions give additive equivalences with ℕ and ℤ, with finite-coordinate and all-integer regular-generator inverses. Scalar extension along arbitrary unital maps between division rings preserves both dimensions and induces bijective class and K₀ maps. For a division-ring source and any ring target, the whole induced maps are independent of the chosen scalar homomorphism. Subsingleton rings give trivial class monoids and groups, not division-ring dimension invariants. Every unital ring homomorphism induces additive scalar-extension maps on right-module classes and K₀, with arbitrary-carrier evaluation and entire-map identity and composition laws over noncommutative and zero rings. The free-word zero-generator augmentation returns the coefficient of the empty word, fixing constants and killing letter monomials. The full-letter linear combination has range equal to its canonical semilinear kernel, under the left regular word-semiring action. These results allow arbitrary, possibly noncommutative or trivial coefficient semirings and empty or infinite alphabets, with independent coefficient and alphabet universes. Over a commutative base ring R and an arbitrary target ring S, right scalar extension agrees with the module-first Mathlib tensor product, with the specified homomorphism-induced coefficient action and right multiplication on coefficients. For commutative S, a separate pointwise comparison lands in the right-module view of Mathlib's scalar-first extension. deliverables.name: spectral-stone-duality
deliverables.title: Spectral stone duality
deliverables.description: Prime-ideal spectra of bounded distributive lattices and their contravariant equivalence with spectral spaces. Also proves spectrality of small cofiltered limits with spectral arrows, compact-open cylinder bases and descent over actual limits, and compact-open lifting from arbitrary subspaces of prespectral spaces. Finite labelled families, including empty families, descend to coherent whole-stage covers. Also proves retrocompactness and prespectral, compact, quasi-separated subtype topology for compact locally closed subsets of prespectral quasi-separated spaces, without ambient compactness. These results do not assert sobriety. It also constructs the soberification of any topological space and its reflection into T0 quasi-sober spaces, independently of spectral Stone duality. Every finite irreducible subset of any topological space contains a generic point of its closure, so every finite topological space is quasi-sober, without a separation or nonemptiness assumption. In T0 spaces, the original point is the unique closed point of its generization subspace, without a spectrality assumption. Finite joins in the underlying order category of a distributive lattice with bottom are universal coproducts; disjointness is characterized by pairwise-zero meets at distinct indices. Functors between thin order categories of bounded lattices preserve finite limits and colimits exactly when their object maps are bounded lattice homomorphisms, without distributivity or shared carrier universe. A cofinite space is quasi-sober exactly when its underlying type is finite, including the empty space. For any quasi-sober space, topological Krull dimension equals the order-theoretic Krull dimension of the original points with their specialization preorder, without a T0 assumption. The canonical soberification of every topological space preserves its topological Krull dimension, without quasi-sobriety or separation assumptions on the input.

deliverables.name: valuation-integers
deliverables.title: Valuation Integers
deliverables.description: Power divisibility and a Krull-dimension bound for the integers of a rank-at-most-one valuation, a converse producing rank data from a dimension bound, and intersections of valuation subrings with full residue-field maps. Every finite separable extension of the original residue field is realized by a compatible finite simple field extension of the same degree, with a base-compatible residue isomorphism and corresponding power-basis generators. Finite rank-at-most-one intersections have classified primes, dimension at most one and finite spectra whose nonempty opens contain zero. Finite pairwise inequivalent rank-one intersections have a separately hypothesized generic-point fork homeomorphism. Equivalent surjective valuations of a ring into a common cyclic-unit linearly ordered commutative group with zero are equal. A canonical rank-at-most-one valuative topology detects values less than one by convergence of powers; for division rings, the specified identity homeomorphism recognizes equivalence of two rank-at-most-one valuations. Valuations of rank at most one on division rings also have a real absolute-value construction using the specified rank embedding, with comparison lemmas including trivial valuations. Rank-one valuations give nontrivial absolute values, and the associated absolute values are equivalent exactly when the valuations are, even for different ambient value groups. Dense compatible valued-field extensions induce dense integer algebra maps and bijective residue maps, specializing to a reduction-compatible residue equivalence for the uniform completion at arbitrary valuation rank. A dense ring homomorphism preserving raw values exactly identifies the canonical completion of a valued field with a complete separated valued ring over an arbitrary common value group. Dense exactly value-preserving additive maps of valued rings induce uniformities. Bounded submodules of finite-dimensional normed spaces over complete fields are finitely generated over Noetherian coefficient rings whose images contain the norm unit ball, with an extension-integer application. At a positive even index 2k and a prime p with p - 1 dividing 2k, the divided Bernoulli number B_(2k)/(2k) has additive p-adic valuation -1 - v_p(2k) and positive reduced denominator exponent 1 + v_p(2k). For every integer n and positive natural k, the rational expression n^k * (n^k - 1) * (bernoulli k / k) is integral over the integers. More generally, if n^k * (n^k - 1) * q is integral for every natural n, every prime p in the reduced denominator of q satisfies p - 1 divides k. This includes k = 0 and applies to divided Bernoulli numbers at every index. For Henselian valuation integers, a sharp power-root neighborhood has an exact correction value, and the stock power range in the canonical units topology is open when the exponent has nonzero image in the field. For a valuation v on a field with any linearly ordered commutative value group with zero, assume v.valuationSubring is Henselian at its maximal ideal m. For a polynomial f over that subring and a in it, a strict squared-derivative value inequality gives a root b, the exact error/displacement identity, derivative-value equality and uniqueness throughout the original derivative ball. For every natural s, f(a) in m^(2*s+1) and f'(a) not in m^(s+1) give all these conclusions and b-a in m^(s+1), without completeness, rank, discreteness, Noetherianity, monicity or unit-derivative assumptions. For e, d, z in that subring, two algebraic comparisons require no Henselianity: e in m^(2*s+1) and d not in m^(s+1) imply v(e) < v(d)^2, and under the same hypotheses the identity v(e) = v(d) * v(z) implies z in m^(s+1).

highlights.title: Residue degree bounded by field degree
highlights.html: If R is a valuation domain with fraction field F, L is a finite field extension of F, and a local R-algebra S embeds into L over R with compatible original residue-field actions, then the residue field of S is finite over that of R and its degree is at most the degree of L over F.

highlights.title: Unique residue and field homomorphism lifts
highlights.html: Over a Henselian valuation domain R with fraction field F, if local commutative R-algebras S and T embed in finite field extensions L/F and E/F with compatible given ambient and residue scalar towers, [L : F] = [κS : κR], [E : F] = [κT : κR] and κS/κR separable, then every κR-algebra homomorphism φ from κS to κT lifts uniquely to an R-algebra homomorphism ψ from S to T satisfying residue T (ψ s) = φ (residue S s) for every s in S and admits a unique F-algebra homomorphism ι from L to E with algebraMap T E (ψ s) = ι (algebraMap S L s) for every s in S.

highlights.title: A sharp Hensel criterion at arbitrary valuation rank
highlights.html: Over a Henselian valuation ring, the strict inequality v(f(a)) < v(f'(a))² gives a root with exact error/displacement identity and unchanged derivative value, unique throughout the original derivative ball.

highlights.title: Unit norms over Henselian valuation domains
highlights.html: Let R be a Henselian valuation domain with fraction field F and S a local commutative R-algebra embedded in a finite extension L/F, with compatible given ambient and residue algebras. If field degree equals residue degree and the residue extension is separable, every u with u - 1 in an ideal I contained in the maximal ideal of R is the norm of a unit s of S with s - 1 in the extension of I to S. If the base residue field is finite, every unit of R is the norm of a unit of S, with residue separability derived from finiteness. Neither statement requires a Galois or invertible-degree hypothesis.
